title: Tourtière for the Crew
seoTitle: Tourtière for the Crew | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Savory pork-and-beef pie with warm spice baked for ten
subtitle: Savory pork-and-beef pie with warm spice baked for ten
description: Ground pork and beef simmer with onion, potato, and warm spices until rich and fragrant, then bake inside flaky double-crust pies. Cut into hearty wedges and serve with ketchup and cranberry sauce at the line.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Tourtière for the Crew in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch pork. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Brown the meat
steps.instruction: Cook pork and beef in a large skillet over medium-high heat, breaking up clumps until browned. Drain excess fat, leaving about 2 tablespoons in the pan.

steps.title: Build the filling
steps.instruction: Add onion, potato, and garlic. Cook 8 minutes until softened. Stir in cinnamon, cloves, sage, salt, pepper, and broth. Simmer until moisture mostly evaporates and filling looks thick.

steps.title: Cool the filling
steps.instruction: Spread filling on a sheet pan and cool 30 minutes. Hot filling will destroy your pie crust on contact. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Assemble and bake
steps.instruction: Line two deep pie dishes with crust, fill evenly, top with second crust, crimp edges, cut vents, and brush with egg wash. Bake at 375°F until golden and bubbling, 45–50 minutes. Target oven/smoker temperature: 375°F.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 145°F with a 3-minute rest. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Tourtière for the Crew onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Scale for larger halls
steps.instruction: When cooking for more than 10 firefighters, split into two pans halfway through so the bottom layer does not overcook while the top waits — duplicate mise en place if you double batches.

steps.title: Rest and portion
steps.instruction: Rest pies 15 minutes before cutting into wedges. Serve with ketchup and cranberry sauce at the line. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

proTips: A splash of Worcestershire in the filling adds depth without changing the classic profile.
If bottom crust worries you, blind-bake 8 minutes before filling.
Make one pie spicy with cayenne for the crew that always asks for heat.
tonightSpread: Tourtière wedges with ketchup, cranberry sauce, and a simple pea salad.
Pickled beets on the side for a bright counter to rich meat filling.
leftovers: Reheat wedges in the oven so crust re-crispes—microwave makes it sad.
Crumble cold filling into scrambled eggs for a Quebec-style breakfast shift.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Tourtière is pure Canadian comfort—familiar to northern halls, new to southern crews, and universally satisfying on cold shift nights. Two big pies feed ten with leftovers for the next watch.
mealPrepNotes: Filling can be made a day ahead and chilled. Use deep-dish pie plates or one large half-sheet tray pie for easier portioning. Vent crust well so steam escapes and bottom crust stays crisp.
